algebra_witnesses.basis: A product of two distinct Majorana generators squares to -1, so the occupation stabilizer n_p = (1 + i gamma_2p gamma_2p+1)/2 carries the i explicitly and the real Cl(2n,0) branch of section 3.5 is vacuous for the stabilizers this plan uses. Computed rather than asserted, so an implementation that reached for the real algebra would fail a check.

determinant_excitations.comparison_pool: The same builder with conserve_sz true -- the pool R2b, R3 and every mapping record are built on. Filters A-D are required to reproduce exactly the set that builder keeps.
determinant_excitations.statement: Anti-Hermitian singles and doubles against the reference determinant, built WITHOUT the conserve_sz argument the mapping records pass, so that filter B has something to remove and its agreement with the builder's own exclusion is measurable.

majorana_monomials.max_degree_basis: Degree 4 is the cap matched to the rank-2 excitation family every mapping record uses: a rank-r determinant excitation is a combination of Majorana monomials of degree up to 2r. The record reports a degree sweep beside it so the dependence on this cap is visible rather than assumed, and any statement comparing the two pools is made only at the matched cap.
majorana_monomials.statement: Hermitian Majorana monomials of degree 0..4 over the 2n generators, in index order. This is section 3.5's own 'Majorana-generated candidate pool' taken literally.
majorana_monomials.why_not_the_excitation_pool_alone: A pool that has parity, particle number and S_z imposed at construction cannot measure what filters A and B remove: it would report zero marginals, and a reader could not tell a vacuous filter from a pre-filtered pool. The wide pool is what makes A and B measurable at all.

character_probe.basis: One non-reference character, run on the same pool, whose survivor set must differ from the ground-state one. This does not target an excited state or claim anything about section 7.4's track; it demonstrates that the character is a live parameter and that B is not a hard-coded ground-state test.
character_probe.finding: The character is a live parameter at the filter that owns it: B admits a different population under the declared character than under the reference's. But the declared restriction arm fixes its stabilizer signs from the *reference* sector, so filter C then annihilates every candidate B admitted under a different character, and the chain returns an empty admissible pool rather than an error. The character and the restriction arm are therefore not independent declarations -- section 7.4's excited-state track needs both moved together, and a G1 that let them drift would close that track at filter C while section 3.5B's requirement at filter B still looked satisfied. Recorded here because it is cheaper to find at this gate than inside a phase built on top of it.

claim_boundary: Structural scope-decision evidence only, on three declared instances at one degree cap, one reference determinant each, and one restriction arm. Every quantity is a candidate count or an exact action on a computational determinant -- Pauli words applied to basis states, so the action layer is exact up to the candidates' own coefficients -- compared to tolerance by the checker rather than in exact arithmetic. Nothing is sampled, no energy is computed, and no resource quantity is produced. The filters are pre-encoding in the sense that none of them consults the fermion-to-qubit encoding: each is a function of the Majorana index data, the declared conserved quantities and the reference. They are NOT computed in some encoding-free representation -- this package's only arithmetic substrate is the Jordan-Wigner Pauli image, as CONVENTIONS.md states -- and no wording upgrading that may survive review. A marginal reported here is a property of the declared pool: a filter that removes nothing from a pool built with that filter already applied has measured the pool, not the filter, and the record pairs every marginal with the pool it was taken on. This record may retire or sustain the G programme's falsifier; it may not establish that any pool is cheaper to measure, that GA contributes to any resource quantity, or that a smaller Hilbert space exists.

degree_sweep.basis: The Majorana pool's action-equivalence class count against its degree cap, on beh2 only. It bounds what the matched-cap comparison does and does not say: the pools coincide at the matched cap, and the Majorana pool reaches strictly more determinants above it because it is a wider pool, not because a filter found something.

estimand.name: G1_per_filter_marginal_of_the_pre_encoding_restriction_chain
estimand.question: Applied in the declared order A, B -> D -> C -> E, how many candidates does each filter of PLAN.md section 3.5 remove, and does filter E -- the one filter with no post-encoding analogue -- remove anything the package's existing post-encoding filters keep?
estimand.why_it_exists: Section 3.5 is a contract with no quantitative content until this record exists, and section 14 says so. QG1 asks whether pre-encoding algebraic restriction has independent content or is a reformulation of filtering the package already performs. The falsifier for the whole G programme is that filters A-D reproduce the existing filters AND E removes nothing, and it is cheaper to test that here than after G2 has been built on top of it.

gates.abcd_gate_statement: On the same pool and instance, the survivors of A, B, D and C must be exactly the set the package's existing post-encoding machinery accepts: a candidate is accepted there when reference_sector_leakage returns zero target-sector leakage and does not raise on an annihilated reference. Disagreement in either direction is a bug in one of the two paths and blocks the phase; it is not a finding.
gates.e_marginal_gate_statement: Filter E is the only filter with no post-encoding analogue, so its marginal is never folded into an aggregate. The record also carries the number of distinct Pauli words entering E, under the package's own scalar_free_key identity, so that a removal cannot be explained by duplicate words.
gates.no_cost_fields_statement: This tier prices nothing. A record carrying a shot count, a device cost, a C(epsilon) or a k* has changed what it claims and the checker fails it.
gates.restriction_gate_statement: Filter C runs through clifford_qc.subspace.restriction.Restriction.transport, which moves the Hamiltonian, the reference and the candidates together. The congruence rule of section 3.5 then holds by construction rather than by review, and R4's contextual-subspace comparator shares the one implementation.

qg1.falsifier_statement: Filters A-D agree with the existing post-encoding filters AND the action-equivalence quotient E removes nothing -- in which case section 3.5 is a reformulation and G2/G3 do not run.
qg1.what_this_does_not_license: No resource claim of any kind, and no statement that either pool is cheaper to measure. E's marginal on the Majorana pool is a property of that pool: it removes redundancy the excitation builder never creates, so it may not be reported as a reduction of the pool the mapping records use. Nothing here establishes a smaller Hilbert space, and the pre-encoding claim is only that no filter consults the encoding.
qg1.what_was_measured: Filters A-D reproduce the existing post-encoding accept set exactly, on both pools and every declared instance, which is the agreement G1's first gate requires and not a finding. Filter E's marginal splits by pool: it removes candidates from the wide Majorana pool section 3.5 specifies, over entrants that are all distinct Pauli words, and it removes nothing from the excitation pool the mapping and cost records are built on. At the matched degree cap the surviving Majorana classes reach exactly the determinants the excitation pool reaches, so the chain reconstructs that pool rather than producing a different or smaller one.

restriction_arm.basis: Filter C is evaluated through the shipped Restriction primitive rather than a second implementation of P_s A P_s, which is G1's third gate. parity+2q is the declared arm that actually fixes stabilizer qubits -- two of them -- so the filter has a non-empty fixing set to act through; an identity restriction would make C vacuous by construction rather than by measurement.

pool_correspondence_at_the_matched_cap.basis: The E-class representatives of the wide Majorana pool against the identity plus the excitation pool the mapping records use. Equality here means the pre-encoding chain reconstructs the pool the package already builds rather than a different or smaller one, which is the fact G2 turns on.

e_marginal.basis: Every candidate entering E is a distinct Pauli word under the package's own scalar_free_key identity when removal_is_not_word_deduplication is true, so no removal here is a duplicate word being collapsed. E is quotienting the physical action on the reference, which is what section 3.5E claims and what no existing code path performs.
e_marginal.mechanism: On the Majorana pool the collapse is not mysterious and should not be reported as though it were. i gamma_2p gamma_2p+1 = 2 n_p - 1 is a stabilizer of any determinant, so a monomial and that monomial times an occupation stabilizer drive the reference in the same direction while being different Pauli words -- and a degree-4 pool contains both. That is precisely section 3.5E's 'A and A S_alpha generate the same physical direction', and it is why the marginal is large here and zero on a pool whose builder never emits the stabilizer multiples. The number measures the pool's redundancy, not a compression of anything the project measures.

gate_abcd_versus_existing_pauli_filters.pauli_side_path: clifford_qc.subspace.symmetry.reference_sector_leakage == 0, with the annihilated-reference exception counted as a rejection

global_centralizer_contrast.basis: Section 3.5B: [A,Q]=0 is sufficient for sector preservation and not necessary. Hard-coding it would fail this phase's first gate by exactly this many candidates and would foreclose section 7.4's excited-state track, which needs a declared character rather than unconditional commutation.

stages.statement: parity / even subalgebra: keep A with [A, (-1)^N] = 0
conserved-quantity character: keep A with (Q - q_target) A psi_ref = 0 for every declared Q, which is the reference-conditioned form of the centralizer and not the global commutant

detail.clause_overlap_with_B: B precedes D and tests the same character on the same action, so leaves_target_sector is expected to be 0 here. It is reported rather than dropped because its value is what shows the two filters overlap, and standalone_removals records what D's containment clause removes on its own.

target_character.parameter_basis: Section 3.5B requires this to be a parameter from the first commit, because an implementation that hard-codes the ground-state character -- or the stronger global condition [A,Q]=0 -- forecloses the excited-state track of section 7.4. excited_character_probe below exercises a different declared character on the same pool so the parameter is demonstrated live rather than asserted.
target_character.statement: Filter B requires (Q - q_target) A psi_ref = 0 for Q in {N, S_z}, with q_target defaulting to the reference determinant's own character.

why_instances_share_their_counts: The declared instances sit in one (N=4, S_z=0) sector on eight qubits, and every filter is a function of that sector's structure rather than of the Hamiltonian, so equal marginals across them are expected. The reference determinant does enter: beh2 and h4 share an occupied set and so share their surviving labels, while hubbard_2x2 fills (0,3,4,7) and its surviving label set differs. Equal counts with differing labels is the signature to look for; equal labels across different occupied sets would be the defect.
